clue.text: Relatively simple tip to make moonshine

parts.note: bald means plain or unadorned, so 'relatively simple' is the comparative, balder
to dash is to throw or tip out, as in dashing water from a bucket

explanation.surface: A recipe for home-distilled liquor with one easy trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonshine' looks like illicit whisky, but here it is the other sense: foolish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine can mean nonsense or empty talk, which is exactly what balderdash is.

clue.text: Biden's necessary male

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 'the necessary' is slang for money, and an American president's money is the dollar
second meaning: the male of deer, rabbits and similar animals

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Truman's 'The buck stops here' on a president's desk; really it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck is US slang for a dollar, and it is also the name for a male deer or rabbit.

clue.text: Way back in penalty

indicators.note: back tells us to read the run of letters found in the next word from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the word penalty

explanation.surface: A traffic offence costing you points or a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks ENAL out of penALty, and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a narrow road, a way from one place to another.

clue.text: Former southern facility set up spear carriers?

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: set up, in a down clue, means the word for facility is written bottom to top

parts.note: art is skill or facility at something

explanation.surface: A disused southern installation erected for men carrying spears.
explanation.walkthrough: A spear carrier in theatre is a walk-on actor with no lines; the question mark marks this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Spear carriers are minor non-speaking performers, the stage equivalent of film extras.

clue.text: Pull that counts out the sine qua non of chilling drum?

definitions.text: the sine qua non of chilling drum?

parts.note: a draught is a pull or swig of drink, and also a pull on a cart
an excluder is something that leaves things out or counts them out

explanation.surface: Something about a pull and a drum that won't let you play.
explanation.walkthrough: Drum is old slang for a house or home, and chilling here is relaxing; a draught excluder is a long fabric sausage laid against a door to stop cold air getting in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy, relaxing home needs to keep out cold air, and that device blocking door gaps is essential for it.

clue.text: Primarily shady and dingy? No, the reverse

indicators.note: primarily means take only the first letter of the next word

parts.note: dingy means dark, poorly lit, which is unlit

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a place is shady and dingy and is told it is the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is S plus UNLIT; the definition is 'No, the reverse', the opposite of shady and dingy.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of a shady, gloomy place is one bathed in bright daylight.

clue.text: After head of garlic peeled, old lamb is next item in rogan josh recipe

definitions.text: next item in rogan josh recipe

indicators.note: after places the next part behind that first letter
head of means the first letter of garlic
peeled means the outer letters are stripped off like skin

parts.note: a lamb that has grown old is a sheep

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions for an Indian curry: peel the garlic, then add the lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: Peeling SHEEP of its outer letters leaves HEE, which goes after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarified butter is the usual cooking fat in Indian dishes such as this lamb curry.

clue.text: Mad Hatter husband to hijack hunk?

indicators.note: mad says the letters of the word Hatter and the husband's letter are jumbled

parts.note: to hijack is to rob a vehicle

explanation.surface: Alice's Mad Hatter turns into a husband carjacking a good-looking man.
explanation.walkthrough: HATTER is rearranged to HEARTT, then H and ROB follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-throb is an attractive man who sets hearts racing, just like a hunk.

clue.text: Pop in power hike? It's a concern

parts.note: to pop in is to enter
P is the physics symbol for power
a hike is a rise, as in a pay hike

explanation.surface: An electricity price increase is worrying news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' looks like worry, but it means a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern is a business or firm, and so is an enterprise.

clue.text: Trick is not commonly behind straight embarrassment

indicators.note: behind puts the colloquial word after the straight's letters

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
ain't is the common, nonstandard form of is not

explanation.surface: A prank that isn't straightforward causes awkwardness.
explanation.walkthrough: Ain't is the colloquial contraction of 'is not', hence 'commonly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Constraint is awkward restraint or self-consciousness, a feeling close to embarrassment.

clue.text: Hand gin back?

indicators.note: back tells us to write the word for gin from right to left

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: Someone asks for their gin to be passed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink but is the old word for a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a hand in something is to have a part in it, a share or role.

clue.text: Line in which cop moves with caution

indicators.note: moves says the letters of cop and caution shift around into a new order

explanation.surface: A police officer carefully patrols his beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' is a line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Your line of work is your job or profession, the trade you follow.

clue.text: Bravo! In attack Caesar's killing time with male attendant

parts.note: Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in says the time and male letter go inside the word for attack

parts.note: a raid is an attack
Julius Caesar was killed on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: A cheer as an assault times Caesar's murder with a man's help.
explanation.walkthrough: IDES and M go inside RAID after its R, giving RIDESMAID, all after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid is a woman who attends the bride at a wedding.

clue.text: This will presumably preclude profit

parts.note: to bar is to prevent or preclude
gain is profit

explanation.surface: A cheap deal leaves the seller little profit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the word splits into 'bar gain', which would stop profit; a cheap buy also gives the seller no profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is something sold cheaply, so the seller makes little or nothing on it.

clue.text: Promise to take the plunge with girl gathering rhubarb

indicators.note: gathering means the girl's name gathers the nonsense word inside it

parts.note: Beth is a girl's name
rhubarb is slang for nonsense, which is rot

explanation.surface: A girl with rhubarb vows to get married.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the plunge is marrying; rhubarb is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To betroth is to promise someone in marriage, an engagement to wed.

clue.text: In particular in a maladroit fashion?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read whimsically: done without skill, the negative word followed by the adverb of being able

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOT ABLY to see the playful second meaning, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Notably means especially or specifically, the same as in particular.

clue.text: Swears about replacing opener in pockets

indicators.note: replacing opener says the first letter of the pockets word gives way to the about letter

parts.note: purses are small pockets or pouches for money
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone swears while fumbling about in their pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: C replaces the P at the start of PURSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to swear, use bad language.

clue.text: What gets Tarka going? He is one who is into upcycling?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Tarka is the otter of Henry Williamson's novel, and his name starts with T, so T plus otter whimsically names what starts him

definitions.text: He is one who is into upcycling?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rag-and-bone man who collects scrap for reuse

explanation.walkthrough: Tarka the Otter is a classic English children's novel; totting is British slang for scavenging scrap to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A totter recovers discarded junk and gives it new value, a forerunner of the modern recycler.

clue.text: When rude theatre plays becoming seedy

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters of the three words frolic about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Watching vulgar theatre makes one feel grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy' looks like sordid but means unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy, in British usage, means slightly ill, the same as feeling poorly.

clue.text: People who are valuable when facing exclusive groups

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sets are exclusive social circles, as in the jet set

explanation.surface: Valuable people mixing with cliques.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable person, as in 'she is an asset to the team'.

clue.text: PDQ closing, e.g., Murray's bar

indicators.note: closing means the soon word closes round the name

parts.note: PDQ, pretty damn quick, means soon
Al is an example of someone called Murray, the comedian Al Murray

explanation.surface: Last orders at a pub belonging to a man named Murray.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Murray is a British comedian famous as the Pub Landlord, which suits the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a bar, either a saloon bar in a British pub or a Wild West drinking house.

clue.text: Rotating bobbins for light boats

indicators.note: rotating means the word for bobbins is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: bobbins are spools for thread

explanation.surface: Spinning reels on a sailing boat's rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a small single-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Viceroy posed with charge

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat means posed
a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: A governor who sat for a portrait while facing a criminal charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, ruling on the king's behalf.

clue.text: Lobby every wife in home of literary festival

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the town's name

parts.note: Hay-on-Wye in Wales hosts a famous literary festival
all means every

explanation.surface: Every wife lobbying at a book festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Hay-on-Wye, usually just Hay, is a Welsh book town with a big annual literary festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is an entrance hall or corridor in a building, the same as a hallway.

clue.text: Bitter end of uncoated tablet

parts.note: IPA, India pale ale, is a bitter beer

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of uncoated

explanation.surface: A pill without a coating leaves a bitter taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tablet' looks like a pill but is the Apple computer.
explanation.definitionFit: An iPad is Apple's brand of tablet computer.

clue.text: Ascot, say, covering onset of racing row

indicators.note: covering, in a down clue, puts the tie on top of the next letter

parts.note: an ascot is a kind of broad tie or cravat

indicators.note: onset of means the first letter of racing

explanation.surface: A seating row at Ascot racecourse as racing begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is the famous racecourse, but here it is the cravat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row of seats, one of several rising levels.

clue.text: Give in and hit the hay around noon

indicators.note: around means the bed word goes around the noon letter

parts.note: to hit the hay is to go to bed

explanation.surface: Surrendering to tiredness and sleeping at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend is to yield or submit, giving way under pressure.

clue.text: Iffy skirt preceding row

indicators.note: preceding puts the skirt word before the row word

parts.note: to skirt is to border, edge around
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A questionable skirt worn ahead of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Borderline means uncertain, only just acceptable, which is iffy.

clue.text: On ice, finally, slip carelessly, causing swelling

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, means the letter goes after the slip word

parts.note: to nod is to make a careless slip, as when 'Homer nods'

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of ice

explanation.surface: Slipping over on ice gives a lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' suggests falling but here it is nod, a lapse of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knob or lump, such as a swollen lymph node.

clue.text: Happily Peru will adopt new cut in crude

indicators.note: will adopt means the jumbled Peru takes the new letter in
happily suggests the letters of Peru are rearranged by chance

parts.note: pared means cut or trimmed

explanation.surface: Peru takes on new oil-sector cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Peru becomes UPRE, which takes in N to give UNPRE, before PARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude means raw or unprocessed, not refined or made ready.
